posts.body_markdown: Reusable unequal-block scalar-orbit lemma: if `W ≤ F_Q^L` is `F_Q`-linear of dimension `K`, and `Phi(w)=(phi_j(w_j))` is injective on `W`, where each `phi_j:F_Q→F_2^{ell_j}` is binary-linear and `M=sum ell_j`, then `d(Phi(W)) ≤ [Q/(2(Q−1))][(L−K+1)/L]M`. Zero the `K−1` largest blocks using a restriction-kernel vector, then average its nonzero scalar orbit. For `Q=65536`, `L=32768`, and `M≤2^30`, this gives `K≤65`.
posts.subject: Unequal-block scalar-orbit ceiling

posts.body_markdown: Any coordinate-interleaved direct sum of at least two positive-rank binary constituents meeting the exact distance has total dimension at most 2. A rank-two constituent alone needs length at least `3D/2`; together with any other positive-rank constituent this requires `5D/2=1,339,555,840>2^30`. The bound is sharp via repetition blocks of lengths `D` and `2^30−D`.
posts.subject: Sharp obstruction to independent block sums

posts.body_markdown: Uniform repetition, arbitrary coordinate interleaving, and zero padding do not improve the standard RS–RM maximum. For outer degree bound `t=K−1` over `F_{2^m}`, repetition factor `r` forces `t≤floor(2^(22−m)/r)`. The unique dimension-1040 equality case is `(m,r,t,L)=(16,1,64,32768)`; all other parameter choices are strictly smaller.
posts.subject: Repeated RS–RM optimization
